ko.text: The outage overruns by no more than 3 days – the grid is counting on the plant

top.text: The project buffer doesn't end up in the red

name: Power Plant Outage
tagline: A unit overhaul in a fixed window
scope: Preparation and orders, unit shutdown, turbine inspection, pipe replacement, control system update, pressure tests and restart. Procedures are prescribed by standards and equipment manufacturers.
approachText: Clear and stable requirements, prescribed procedures, a fixed window and a high price for every change. The whole project is best managed predictively: a stage-by-stage plan, a detailed Gantt with a critical path, change and risk management. Agile practices would mostly be overhead here.
intro: You're managing the planned overhaul of a power plant unit. From preparation to restart you have 46 working days – and every extra day costs millions.

workstreams.name: Outage schedule and contractor coordination
workstreams.why: Dozens of contractors must take turns in an exact order. Without an upfront plan they'd trip over each other and the window wouldn't be enough.

workstreams.name: Turbine inspection per the manufacturer's procedure
workstreams.why: The manufacturer prescribes the inspection step by step. Nothing "emerges" here – you follow the plan.

workstreams.name: Replacement of worn piping
workstreams.why: The scope is known from measurements and parts are ordered months ahead. Classic planned work.

workstreams.name: Control system software update
workstreams.why: Careful – even though it's software, it's a certified vendor release deployed and tested by an approved procedure. You don't iterate, you plan.

workstreams.name: Workplace safety and work permits
workstreams.why: The rules come from regulations and every permit is formally issued in advance.

workstreams.name: Parts, tools and scaffolding logistics
workstreams.why: What must arrive, when and where follows directly from the work schedule.

workstreams.name: Operator training on new equipment
workstreams.why: The content is set by the equipment changes and the deadline is fixed – operators must be ready before the restart.

workstreams.name: Pressure tests and unit restart
workstreams.why: Tests follow a procedure and criteria set by standards. No room for experiments.

phases.name: Preparation
phases.goal: Plan, orders, contractor agreements, scaffolding and training.

tasks.name: Detailed schedule and permits
tasks.note: Without an approved plan nothing can be ordered or contracted.

tasks.name: Parts order
tasks.note: What exactly to order comes out of the detailed plan.

tasks.name: Contracts with work contractors
tasks.note: The plan defines the contractors' scope of work.

tasks.name: Scaffolding erection
tasks.note: Built by the in-house crew from a standard design.

tasks.name: Contractor safety training
tasks.note: Contractor staff get trained – so their contracts must already be signed.

tasks.name: Parts and tools staging
tasks.note: Getting ready what was ordered.

phases.name: Shutdown and disassembly
phases.goal: Safely shut down the unit, let it cool and open up the equipment.

tasks.name: Unit shutdown
tasks.note: The very first step of the outage.

tasks.name: Equipment cooldown
tasks.note: Only a shut-down unit can cool off.

tasks.name: Insulation removal
tasks.note: Hands off hot pipes.

tasks.name: Weld inspection
tasks.note: Welds are only accessible once the insulation is off.

tasks.name: Turbine casing removal
tasks.note: The turbine has to cool down first, too.

phases.name: Repairs and replacements
phases.goal: Turbine inspection, new piping, boiler and control system repairs.

tasks.name: Turbine inspection
tasks.note: The longest job of the stage; the turbine was opened in the last one.

tasks.name: Pipe replacement
tasks.note: The old piping is stripped of insulation and ready to go.

tasks.name: Boiler repair
tasks.note: The boiler has been accessible since the last stage.

tasks.name: Control system update
tasks.note: Vendor software, deployed on the shut-down unit.

tasks.name: Welding and testing new joints
tasks.note: Welding the newly fitted pipe sections.

tasks.name: New insulation installation
tasks.note: Insulation goes on the finished piping and the repaired boiler.

phases.name: Tests and restart
phases.goal: Verify everything is tight and working, and put the unit back on the grid.

tasks.name: Pressure tests
tasks.note: Verify that the new piping and boiler don't leak.

tasks.name: Control system test
tasks.note: Simulating operating states on the new software.

tasks.name: Unit restart
tasks.note: Restart only with verified tightness and tested controls.

tasks.name: Trial operation
tasks.note: Monitoring the running unit.

tasks.name: Handover documentation
tasks.note: Written continuously from test reports, doesn't wait for the equipment.

gate.title: Checkpoint review: outage halfway
gate.text: Plant management is checking whether the outage is on plan and whether the unit will restart on time. How do you prepare?
gate.lesson: A checkpoint in a predictive project is about the exact status against the plan: critical path, buffer burn, risks and truly finished work.

choices.text: Critical path status, buffer burn and top risks + an on-site tour of finished work
choices.feedback: Management sees the exact status and approved a stronger night shift where slippage looms.

choices.text: A presentation saying everything is "green"
choices.feedback: The director asked about one specific job and the answer didn't match the slides. Trust is gone.

choices.text: Cancel the checkpoint review, we don't have time
choices.feedback: Management started finding out the status on its own – by touring the foremen on site.

events.title: Crack in a pipe
events.text: Non-destructive testing found a crack in one pipe that nobody expected. Fixing it means extra work.
events.lesson: Even a predictive project hits surprises. New work gets in through change control, with its impact on the critical path assessed.

choices.text: Change control: add the repair to the plan and assess the critical path impact
choices.feedback: The repair was scheduled off the critical path. The stage stretches by a day at most.

choices.text: Keep quiet, the pipe will last a few more years
choices.feedback: The inspector found the crack in the test report. Now there's a special audit of the whole project.

choices.text: Fix it now and pull people off other work
choices.feedback: The repair is underway, but other work has stalled – including work on the critical path.

events.title: No certified welder
events.text: The contractor moved its only welder certified for high-pressure piping to another job.
events.lesson: A risk register with prepared responses (e.g. backup contractors) turns a crisis into routine.

choices.text: Call in the backup contractor from the risk register
choices.feedback: The backup contractor was vetted in advance. A welder showed up the next day.

choices.text: Poach a welder from a competitor at triple the rate
choices.feedback: It works, but it's expensive and shaky.

choices.text: Let an uncertified worker do the welding
choices.feedback: The welds failed inspection and must be redone. And a fine is looming.

choices.text: Wait for the welder to come back
choices.feedback: Pipe work is stalled, and everything that follows with it.

events.title: Turbine blades arrive late
events.text: The manufacturer reports the replacement turbine blades will arrive a week late.
events.lesson: If you know the critical path, you know what can be reshuffled and what can't – and one late delivery doesn't have to move the project end.

choices.text: Reshuffle work off the critical path so the float absorbs the delay
choices.feedback: The team pulled work with float forward. The project end didn't budge.

choices.text: Pay for air freight
choices.feedback: The blades arrived on time – for the price of a small car.

choices.text: Wait for the blades
choices.feedback: The turbine inspection is on the critical path – a week of waiting pushes the whole project.

choices.text: Use the old blades and replace them "some other time"
choices.feedback: The manufacturer refused to warranty the turbine.

events.title: "While we have it all apart…"
events.text: Management wants to use the outage to also replace the lighting in the whole hall and the camera system.
events.lesson: In a predictive project the scope is fixed. Every extra request goes through change control – even the one that "costs nothing".

choices.text: Change control: assess the impact and add only what fits off the critical path
choices.feedback: Lighting will be done next outage; the cameras fit into the float.

choices.text: Add everything to the plan
choices.feedback: Management is happy, but a big chunk of work just landed in an already tight plan.

choices.text: Refuse without assessment
choices.feedback: The plan is protected, but management feels brushed off.

events.title: Fatigue on the shifts
events.text: Shifts have been running 12 hours a day for weeks on end. Small mistakes are piling up.
events.lesson: Fatigue is a safety risk. Even in a fixed window it pays to respect shift limits and keep spare capacity.

choices.text: Respect shift limits and reinforce the night shift
choices.feedback: Mistakes dropped and people have the energy for the final push.

choices.text: Add even more overtime
choices.feedback: The next week: two injuries and one serious assembly error.

choices.text: Give time off only after the unit restart
choices.feedback: People will hang in there, but the mistakes aren't going away.

events.title: Near miss on the scaffolding
events.text: A wrench fell off the scaffolding and missed a fitter by a meter. Nobody got hurt.
events.lesson: Near misses are free warnings. Investigate without blame and adjust the procedure.

choices.text: Stop scaffolding work, investigate the cause blamelessly and adjust the procedure
choices.feedback: The scaffolding got nets and tool boxes. People see that safety is taken seriously.

choices.text: Carry on, nothing happened
choices.feedback: A week later, something heavier fell.

choices.text: Punish the fitter who dropped the wrench
choices.feedback: Nobody reports near misses anymore.

events.title: The grid wants the unit sooner
events.text: The transmission system operator asks to restart the unit two days early because of an expected cold-snap peak.
events.lesson: Shortening a deadline is assessed on the critical path. Cutting tests and inspections for speed doesn't pay off.

choices.text: Check the critical path and offer a partial-load restart without cutting tests
choices.feedback: The grid operator got partial output early and full output on time.

choices.text: Promise an earlier restart and shorten the tests
choices.feedback: The tests were rushed and a valve burst during the restart.

choices.text: Refuse
choices.feedback: The plan holds, but the relationship with the grid operator took a hit.
